topSignals.title: FuelCell Energy names a new CFO and reaffirms its Q4 FY2027 profitability target, citing AI/data-center demand as the growth driver.
topSignals.text: Matthew Latino (previously SVP Finance/Segment CFO at Xylem) took over as CFO on October 7, 2026, succeeding Michael Bishop after 15 years; Bishop stays on as a senior advisor through the 2027 annual meeting. The company reaffirmed its target of reaching positive Adjusted EBITDA in Q4 of fiscal 2027, contingent on ramping annualized production, converting awarded-to-committed backlog, and cost reduction — and explicitly named AI/data-center demand for reliable, always-on power as what is driving its commercial pipeline. GlobeNewswire

topSignals.title: Virginia's new 2026 Energy Plan names fuel cells the preferred near-term reliability technology, creating a dedicated up-to-5 GW category — and it is only now surfacing in sell-side coverage.
topSignals.text: The Virginia Department of Energy's "Clean-First, Least-Cost" plan (released Oct 1) defines a new "non-combustion gas resource" category built for fuel cells, targeting up to 5 GW of deployment in a 2029-2035 window, citing faster build times (18-24 months vs. years for gas plants), lower local emissions/noise, and distribution-level interconnection. RBC Capital (Oct 2, Outperform, $335 PT) and Barclays (early Oct, PT raised to $308 from $276) both cited it in raising Bloom Energy targets; BE traded in the $288-$295 range through the week. This had not yet been logged in this monitor. Benzinga - RBC note, Benzinga - Oct 6 move

topSignals.title: EIA's October 6 Short-Term Energy Outlook lifts the Henry Hub forecast to $3.48/MMBtu (2026) and $3.16/MMBtu (2027) - a fresh LCOE fuel-cost input that supersedes the figures logged through Oct 7.
topSignals.text: This replaces the $2.93/MMBtu summer-2026 average (Sept 25 release) checked yesterday and the earlier $3.50-3.67/MMBtu vintages; the new STEO points to roughly a 9% price decline from 2026 to 2027. Next STEO release: November 10, 2026. EIA STEO

lcoe.text: EIA Oct 6, 2026 STEO - Henry Hub forecast raised to $3.48/MMBtu (2026) and $3.16/MMBtu (2027), a ~9% year-on-year decline. This is the freshest official natural-gas price vintage and supersedes the Sept 25 ($2.93/MMBtu summer-2026) and earlier Jan/Jul 2026 ($3.50-3.67/MMBtu) figures logged previously - use this as the current fuel-cost input. EIA STEO

Virginia's 5 GW 2029-2035 fuel-cell target is a market-sizing/deployment-window datapoint rather than a direct cost figure, but is relevant to addressable-market assumptions for any US-market LCOE/market model extension.
